rule_summary: Adoption subsidies are individually negotiated from $0, based on the youth's needs and family circumstances, with regional maximums.
notes: Third-party summary; may be out of date. Regional per diem range of $26.03 to $47.19 quoted there, not confirmed.

rule_summary: Applicants and licensees must have a valid background check under AS 47.05.300-47.05.390 and 7 AAC 10.900-10.990, screening for barrier crimes or conditions.
notes: Fingerprint detail not found in snippets.

rule_summary: Each child must have space and a specific place for their own clothing and possessions. Infants may not share a bed with an adult (safe sleep rule).
notes: Bedroom sharing rule not found.

rule_summary: Base rate is set from the Federal Poverty Guidelines for Alaska for one person divided by days in the year, adjusted by child age and a geographic cost-of-living differential. Rates rose 30 percent on 1 July 2024.
notes: One OCS rate sheet lists $40.73 per day for ages 12-20; year unclear. Current regional table not found.

rule_summary: The department proposes a base rate change to the legislature at least every five years or when the rate deviates 10 percent or more from the previous rate.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: 7 AAC 67.210 sets maximum capacity. A general variance is needed for more than six children in a foster home.
notes: Section text was truncated in the snippet; record shows effective date 1 July 2022 (not confirmed for this subsection). Unclear whether the six includes the carer's own children.

rule_summary: For children receiving home and community-based waiver services, capacity is limited to three children including the licensee's and household members' own children.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: There are no fees to become a foster parent.
notes: Unclear which result carried this statement; check the page.

rule_summary: A licensing redesign public notice mentions biennial licences and renewals.
notes: Unclear: from a public notice, text not retrieved. Treat the two-year term as unconfirmed.

rule_summary: Foster licence applicants must be at least 21.
notes: Read from search summary. Justia copy may not be the latest version. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: After the first year, foster parents complete training in an individual training plan that the licensing specialist updates each year.
notes: Hours not stated in snippet.

rule_summary: The department may require a foster care orientation or training programme. Orientation covers the practice model and ICWA. First-year licensees are asked to complete Core Training for Resource Families or for Relative Caregivers.
notes: Hour totals not found. Combines regulation and Resource Family Manual summaries.

rule_summary: An applicant or licensee may request a general variance from any requirement of the foster home licensing chapter.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: DHR adoption subsidy policy (Revision 32, effective 1 January 2024) covers a regular subsidy rate and a separate Level One difficulty-of-care rate.
notes: Dollar amounts not extracted. A secondary page lists basic subsidy rates matching foster board rates; not confirmed.

rule_summary: Applicant and each adult household member submit fingerprints to the Alabama Bureau of Investigation for a criminal history check. Chapter 660-5-46 covers checks on current foster parents and household members.
notes: Read from Child Welfare Information Gateway summary (secondary source).

rule_summary: Enough bedrooms for everyone in the home. Children over 6 of the opposite sex must have separate sleeping rooms. Unvented fuel space heaters must be removed from bedrooms and bathrooms.
notes: Read from search summary. Bedroom size rules not found.

rule_summary: Monthly board payment includes a clothing allowance of $20 per month under the administrative code. DHR statistics show an average monthly board payment of about $531.
notes: Average, not a rate schedule. Secondary sites give age-banded rates of about $528 to $571; no official current rate table found.

rule_summary: Caregiver ratios by age apply (one adult per child under 2.5; one per three children aged 2.5 to 6). A home with a compliant unvented fuel space heater may be approved for no more than three foster children.
notes: value 3 is the space-heater limit only. Snippet was cut off, ratios not confirmed in full. An older 2003 rule (660-5-28) capped boarding homes at six children; current overall cap not found.

rule_summary: At initial application the applicant and each adult household member request clearance of the state central registry on child abuse and neglect.
notes: Unclear whether the check repeats at renewal.

rule_summary: DHR adoption policy sets out the application and home study for adoptive applicants.
notes: Content not read; only the existence of the policy chapter is recorded. Model used not found.

rule_summary: A foster family home approval is valid for one year from the date of approval unless revoked or surrendered.
notes: Read from search summary of a mirror copy; check the official code.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 19. One spouse may be under 19 if the couple is related to the child.
notes: Read from search summary of the rule. Unclear whether the same age applies to adoptive applicants; foster and adoptive homes share one approval policy. applies_to may need narrowing to fostering.

rule_summary: A state tax credit of $1,000 applies to adopting a qualified foster child in DHR custody.
notes: From search summary; unclear which result carried the claim. Not checked against statute.

rule_summary: Foster parents may be single or married.
notes: Read from search summary, not the rule text.

rule_summary: Renewal paperwork is due 30 days before the annual approval expires. The agency re-examines the home for continued compliance. An older rule required a physical exam or provider statement every 4 years.
notes: The 4-year physical item is from older chapter 660-5-28 and may be out of date.

rule_summary: 15 hours of in-service training each year after approval.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: 30 hours of preparation training from the approving agency before approval. DHR policy names TIPS (Trauma Informed Partnering for Permanency and Safety) or Deciding Together.
notes: Curriculum name from DHR approval policy (https://dhr.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Foster-Family-Home-Adoptive-Resource-Approval-Policy.pdf). Some secondary pages say MAPP instead; sources disagree on the curriculum name.

rule_summary: Adoption subsidy is set out in DCFS Policy VIII-I (December 2022). A 2013 procedure capped non-recurring adoption expenses at $1,500. Some non-IV-E children may qualify for Medicaid.
notes: Source is the 2014 version of the policy; the $1,500 cap may be out of date. Current 2022 text not read.

rule_summary: Household members 18 and over need a State Police criminal record check and a fingerprint-based FBI check. The head of household certifies in writing that no members aged 10 to 17 have a criminal record.
notes: Certification detail came from a DHS/DCFS-linked summary; unclear which page. Adoption home studies check anyone living in the home more than 3 cumulative months in a year.

rule_summary: Each bedroom should have at least 50 square feet per occupant. No more than four children may share a bedroom. A waiver may be possible for relatives with a 45 square foot room.
notes: From a secondary summary; 45 sq ft waiver from PUB-25 (October 2022). Regulation text not read.

rule_summary: A standard monthly board rate table applies from August 2023. The rate for ages birth to five is $451 a month.
notes: Only the youngest age band read. An October 2022 DCFS publication gave $410 to $500 a month.

rule_summary: A DCFS brochure says no more than five children in the home, including the carer's own.
notes: Brochure date unknown; may be out of date. Hosted by the university training partner.

rule_summary: Household members aged 14 and over must be cleared through the Arkansas Child Maltreatment Central Registry.
notes: value is the minimum age of household members checked.

rule_summary: Older foster home rules require a yearly physical exam for each household member. Adoption rules require an exam within six months before approval and yearly until placement.
notes: 2012 rule; may be out of date.

rule_summary: There may be no roomers or boarders in the home.
notes: Housing tenure (rent or own) rule not found.

rule_summary: A state contract names the SAFE home study for initial home studies and updates, with supervisor review before submission to DCFS.
notes: Procurement listing. Nothing from SAFE content recorded. A DCFS flowchart lists PRIDE and CPR training before approval.

rule_summary: Relatives or fictive kin with a provisional placement have six months from placement to complete full resource home approval.
notes: From a 2022 DCFS relative caregiver handbook; unclear whether it is PUB-14 or PUB-25.

rule_summary: Foster home applicants must be at least 21.
notes: Read from DHS FAQ summary. Adoption minimum age not confirmed.

rule_summary: The Child Welfare Agency Review Board sets minimum licensing standards under the Child Welfare Licensing Act, published as DCFS PUB-04.
notes: Context row.

rule_summary: A single person may apply. Two-parent homes may apply and must show a stable relationship.
notes: Read from DHS FAQ summary.

rule_summary: Resource homes are re-evaluated each year based on the approval date. A 2012 rule required at least quarterly monitoring visits and written notice of the re-evaluation result within 10 days.
notes: Annual re-evaluation from a DCFS flowchart; unclear which DCFS document it is. 2012 items may be out of date.

rule_summary: After approval each foster parent completes at least 15 hours of approved training a year. Online or video training is capped at 5 hours a year with prior approval.
notes: From a 2018 secondary summary; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Family foster parents need at least 30 hours of pre-service training.
notes: From a February 2018 summary; may be out of date. A 2022 DCFS publication lists 12 hours of resource parent training; sources disagree.

rule_summary: Adoption maintenance subsidy may not exceed the foster care payment the child would receive, excluding special allowances. Eligible children may get AHCCCS medical and dental cover.
notes: AHCCCS detail from a secondary summary.

rule_summary: Every adult in the household needs a Level 1 Fingerprint Clearance Card from the Department of Public Safety and must pass FBI and local criminal checks. DCS may waive the card for a kinship foster parent for good cause.
notes: Kinship waiver from DCS 15-07 Kinship Waiver Policy.

rule_summary: Foster parents must provide sufficient space and privacy for a foster child. Sleeping standards are in R21-6-310 and R21-6-311. Children may share bedrooms.
notes: Bedroom rule text (R21-6-310/311) not retrieved. Bedroom-sharing statement came from a secondary page.

rule_summary: Rates are in the DCS Child Placement Rates and Special Allowance Approval Matrix. A 2023 audit report gave $24.60 to $44.69 per day by age and need.
notes: Daily rate, not monthly, so no value recorded. Figures from 2023 auditor report (https://www.azauditor.gov/sites/default/files/2023-11/QA-0703.pdf); may be out of date.

rule_summary: A licence may not exceed five foster children and may be set lower. Increases depend on sleeping arrangements, support network and willingness to care for each extra child.
notes: Counts foster children only, per snippet.

rule_summary: Most contracted licensing agencies charge an $800 adoption certification fee, reimbursed when a waiting Arizona foster child is placed. Waiver or deferment forms exist (AN-058, AN-060).
notes: Fee is charged by contracted private agencies, not DCS. Secondary source; unclear which result carried it.

rule_summary: Adoption applicants provide a physician's report for each parent (DES Form FW-009).
notes: Form name from search summary; form not read.

rule_summary: The licensing agency completes a foster home study and assessment. Adoption needs a formal application and a certification investigation and report.
notes: Adoption part read from DCS policy Chapter 5 Section 17 summary. Model not named.

rule_summary: Applicants may rent or own their home.
notes: From a private agency page in search results, not a DCS source. Unclear which result carried the statement.

rule_summary: The licensing office may waive non-safety requirements case by case for an applicant who will only provide kinship care.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Foster home licences are valid for two years.
notes: 2015 statute version; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Licence states the maximum number and age range of foster children. Changes to capacity, age range or gender need an amendment.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A DCS page says the minimum age is 18 to adopt.
notes: Sources disagree: another page in the same results says 21 or older for both. Unclear which page carried the 18 figure.

rule_summary: Family foster home licence applicants must be at least 21, except under the kinship waiver rule (R21-6-419).
notes: Read from search summary of Cornell LII copy.

rule_summary: Applicants may be single, married or in a relationship. If married, both spouses must complete all requirements.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants must be legal residents of Arizona.
notes: Read from search summary; exact meaning of legal resident not stated.

rule_summary: Renewal requires 12 hours of approved ongoing training in the two-year licence period. Specialised homes need at least 24 hours before renewal.
notes: Sources disagree: a 2015 version of A.R.S. 8-509 says six hours per year. Check current rule.

rule_summary: A 2018 summary of R21-6-303 lists 6 hours of approved initial foster parent training before initial licensure.
notes: From a 2018 secondary summary; may be out of date. DCS policy DCS 15-44 covers pre-service requirements; total pre-service hours may differ.

rule_summary: Adoption Assistance Program rates are adjusted each year by the California Necessities Index with foster care rates. AAP rates for 2026-27 are set in ACL 26-45.
notes: From a Los Angeles County notice. Dollar amounts not read.

rule_summary: Each applicant completes a criminal record statement (RFA 01B). Live Scan fingerprinting is part of the application forms; a valid photo ID is enough to Live Scan.
notes: Combines a Los Angeles County 2019 guide and a CDSS all-county letter. Who in the household is checked not confirmed.

rule_summary: Children of different sexes may not share a bedroom unless each is under 5. Except for infants, children may not share a bedroom with an adult.
notes: From a secondary summary. A low-quality site claimed a limit of two children per bedroom and six per home; not recorded as unconfirmed.

rule_summary: Foster care, Kin-GAP and AAP rates rose by the California Necessities Index (3.42 percent) from 1 July 2025. A county table lists a basic Level of Care rate of $1,301.
notes: County rate table; labels ambiguous, figure unconfirmed. 2026-27 rates are in ACL 26-44 and 26-45, not read, so this is likely out of date.

rule_summary: The total number of children in a resource family home may not exceed six, including the family's own children, unless exceptional circumstances apply. Capacity is set for each home on application review.
legal_citation: Health & Safety Code 1522; Welf. & Inst. Code 16519.61
notes: County page and a secondary summary. Same county page says no more than two children per bedroom.

rule_summary: A licensing agency may authorise up to eight foster children to place siblings or half-siblings together, if conditions in Health and Safety Code 1505.2 are met.
notes: Read from search summary; written for foster family homes, may apply differently to resource families.

rule_summary: A psychosocial assessment and written report evaluate the applicant's capacity to foster, adopt or provide guardianship, based on all information gathered.
notes: Version 3 is older. Model or tool not named in snippets.

rule_summary: Resource Family Approval is one approval combining foster parent licensing, relative approval and approval for adoption and guardianship. It applies to all homes for children in foster care from 1 January 2017.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Secondary guides say resource family applicants must be at least 18. There is no maximum age.
notes: Secondary sources only; regulation text not found. Some counties prefer applicants with more years of adulthood. CDSS FAQ says age requirements are flexible.

rule_summary: Eligibility does not depend on marital status, religion or gender identity. Married, single, separated, divorced, LGBTQ+ and same-sex families may apply.
notes: County page (San Benito), not a state rule.

rule_summary: Approved homes have an annual (12-month) approval update under the Written Directives. Approval stays in effect while the update is pending.
notes: Section number differs by version (8-01 in Version 3). 'Remains in effect' wording from a Santa Clara County handbook. Unclear whether approval has an expiry date.

rule_summary: Approved resource families complete at least 8 hours of training each year, due by the approval anniversary in some county directives.
notes: Read from search summary; version 6.1 may be superseded by Version 8 (November 2022) or later.

rule_summary: Applicants complete at least 12 hours of pre-approval training. Training may start no more than 60 days before the application, and the application must be in before training ends. Some counties require more.
notes: The 60-day detail is from a Los Angeles County copy of Written Directives Version 6. Search pointed to 16519.5; the URL found is for 16519.502 and may not be the right section.

rule_summary: Monthly adoption subsidy may not exceed the foster care maintenance payment the child would have received.
notes: HB26-1373 proposed caps at 50-60 percent of foster care rates from 1 July 2026; passage not confirmed.

rule_summary: Each adult in the home has a background check before full certification, including CBI and FBI fingerprint checks, a CDHS child abuse and neglect check, a TRAILS search and a CBI sex offender check.
notes: List of checks from an agency overview in the same results; read from summaries.

rule_summary: A June 2022 county worksheet lists base foster care rates of $42.02, $53.58 and $65.14 per day by age band (0-8, 9-13, 14+).
notes: Daily rates from a 2022 worksheet on a third-party site; likely out of date. Current FY 2025-26 rate not found.

rule_summary: Up to six children may be placed in a foster home at one time, depending on space and the home study. No more than two children under two, except for sibling groups.
notes: Advocacy FAQ, not regulation. A separate FAQ says no more than ten children including the carer's own; sources may refer to different limits.

rule_summary: State rules must let foster homes exceed capacity and square footage limits to place sibling groups together.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Each foster parent needs a health assessment within 1 year before or 30 days after certification.
notes: From a 2018 secondary summary.

rule_summary: Family foster homes need a hazard-free outdoor play space of at least 75 square feet per child and immediate access to a working telephone.
notes: From a 2018 secondary summary; may be out of date after the 2025 revision of section 7.708.

rule_summary: Applicants may own or rent their home.
notes: County page.

rule_summary: A county page lists being at least 21 as a basic requirement for foster certification.
notes: County page, not a state rule. Regulation text not found.

rule_summary: CDHS memo IM-CW-2025-0060 (effective 12 November 2025) covers changes to all of section 7.708 to align with HB24-1017.
notes: Other Colorado rows may be out of date because of this change.

rule_summary: Applicants may be single, married, divorced, widowed or in a stable domestic partnership.
notes: County page.

rule_summary: Statute provides for certification and annual recertification of foster care homes.
notes: Inferred from the section title only; requirements not read.

rule_summary: Each foster parent completes 20 hours of ongoing training each year, relevant to the children served.
notes: From a 2018 secondary summary.

rule_summary: A rule filing describes 27 hours of pre-certification training, including 12 hours of core training. One county says each adult completes 47 hours in the first year.
notes: Sources disagree and may be out of date. Unclear which filing carried the 27-hour text.

rule_summary: A DCF attachment lists a medically complex (Class 4) subsidised adoption and guardianship rate of $86.10 a day. A general subsidy schedule was not found.
notes: Legislative attachment URL as shown in search results. An undated third-party page gives basic rates of $25.99 to $28.52 a day; likely out of date.

rule_summary: Adult household members need state and national criminal history checks, a national fingerprint-based check, a State Police check and a child protective services history check. New household members are checked before renewal.
notes: Policy effective June 2025. An older policy set the threshold at age 16 and over.

rule_summary: The home needs at least two bedrooms. Foster children may share a room but each needs their own bed. Children of opposite sexes may share a room only until age three.
notes: Citation range is for minimum home standards generally; exact section not confirmed.

rule_summary: Rates effective 1 April 2024 are $27.29 a day for ages 0-5, $27.60 for 6-11 and $29.95 for 12-17 (about $9,961 to $10,930 a year).
notes: Daily rates, so no monthly value recorded. The same report has a second table ($33.27 to $39.40) of unclear category. A May 2026 news report says rates are expected to rise.

rule_summary: Applicants provide a physical exam report from a healthcare provider for everyone in the home.
notes: Unclear which DCF page carried this statement.

rule_summary: The assessment decides whether the applicant can meet sections 17a-145-130 to 160. All applicants attend a ten-week group assessment training, after an open house.
notes: Model not named in DCF sources. A private provider in Connecticut offers TIPS-MAPP, but no DCF source names it.

rule_summary: Applicants must show adequate space for one or more children and sufficient income.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A foster care licence is issued for two years once the applicant meets compliance requirements.
notes: From a June 2017 policy document; may be out of date. Unclear which result carried the statement.

rule_summary: Applicants must be at least 21.
notes: Read from DCF knowledge base summary. Unclear whether the page applies equally to adoption from DCF; DCF licenses foster and prospective adoptive families together.

rule_summary: DCF licenses foster and prospective adoptive families under R.C.S.A. 17a-145-130 to 17a-145-160. Minimum home standards are in 17a-145-137 to 142.
notes: Context row.

rule_summary: A DCF policy document lists Connecticut residency as a requirement.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Each licensed foster or pre-adoptive parent completes 18 hours of post-licensing training each year.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants complete a ten-week group assessment training before licensing.
notes: value is weeks (no weeks unit). Total hours not found.

rule_summary: Licensing requires a criminal records check. CFSA may license a person despite a conviction if set conditions are met after review.
notes: Who in the household is checked not confirmed.

rule_summary: Rules cover basement bedrooms, sharing with an adult, and sharing with an opposite-sex child or one of a large age gap. A foster child's bedroom may not require passing through another sleeping area.
notes: Excerpt cut off before the specific conditions and square footages.

rule_summary: Chapter 60 has a section on foster home capacity (6005).
notes: Text not retrieved; number not recorded.

rule_summary: Licensing requires a Child Protection Register check.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Steps are application, pre-service training, home study, documents, then a foster licence.
notes: Model not named.

rule_summary: A foster parent must have enough family income to meet the household's reasonable needs without relying on foster care board payments.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Kin homes may receive a temporary licence under a separate CFSA policy.
notes: Content not read.

rule_summary: CFSA re-evaluates each resource parent and foster home every two years.
notes: Rule title says annual re-evaluation but snippet text says every two years; sources disagree within the rule.

rule_summary: There is no maximum age.
notes: Secondary source.

rule_summary: A foster parent must be at least 21.
notes: applies_to both because CFSA licenses adoptive families as foster homes first (adoption fact sheet); unclear for non-foster adoption.

rule_summary: Couples or single people can be licensed foster parents.
notes: From a 2012-archived national summary; may be out of date and not DC-specific.

rule_summary: The process takes about five months from the start of pre-service training.
notes: CFSA fact sheet; date unknown.

rule_summary: Resource parents complete 30 hours of in-service training in each two-year licence period. No more than nine online hours count.
notes: 30 hours per two years is from the 2015 policy and a newsletter; 9-hour online cap from the 2022 policy. An older guide mentions 15 hours for a one-year licence.

rule_summary: Applicants complete at least 30 hours of pre-service resource parent training.
notes: 2022 policy. Curriculum not named in snippet.

rule_summary: Basic adoption assistance rates are $396.63 a month for ages 0-9, $451.38 for 10-15 and $510.70 for 16 and over. Payment may not exceed the child's foster care rate.
notes: Third-party summary of a Delaware manual; effective date unknown. Three age bands, so no single value recorded.

rule_summary: Applicants undergo fingerprint-based state and FBI criminal checks.
notes: From a secondary summary of adoption home study rules, citing older numbering. Who in the household is checked not confirmed.

rule_summary: Same-sex children may share a bedroom. Opposite-sex children may share only under age five. A child over one may not share with an adult unless a health care provider documents the need.
notes: Chapter 936 regulates child placing agencies and their foster homes. Unclear whether it governs homes approved directly by DFS, which follow DFS Policy 1302.

rule_summary: A 2019 proposed amendment would cap children in foster care in a family foster home at six, with an exception for a parenting youth and their child.
legal_citation: 9 DE Admin. Code 201 (now 14 DE Admin. Code 936)
notes: Proposed rule; adoption not confirmed.

rule_summary: A child protection registry check by DSCYF is part of the home study.
notes: Adoption home study source; foster equivalent not confirmed.

rule_summary: There is no charge to become a foster parent.
notes: Secondary source.

rule_summary: DFS lists seven steps: portal registration, orientation, training, application, family assessment, final review, then fostering.
notes: Assessment model not named.

rule_summary: Applicants must rent or own their home.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants must be economically stable.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A 2016 flyer said applicants must be no older than 65.
notes: Likely out of date; the current state page summary lists no upper age.

rule_summary: Applicants must be at least 21.
notes: Read from search summary of the state page. A 2016 University of Delaware flyer also gave an upper age of 65; not on the state page.

rule_summary: Applicants must provide references.
notes: Number of references not stated.

rule_summary: Applicants may be single, married, divorced or widowed.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Agency staff inspect the foster home each year against the home requirements.
notes: Licence term not found.

rule_summary: An agency must ensure each foster parent receives at least 12 hours of training a year related to the children's needs.
legal_citation: 9 DE Admin. Code 201 (now 14 DE Admin. Code 936)
notes: From a 2018 summary citing older numbering; current text of 936-II-37.0 not confirmed.

rule_summary: Pre-service training is 27 hours, according to a news report.
notes: News source, not a DFS page.

rule_summary: Lead agencies may negotiate a maintenance adoption subsidy up to 100 percent of the statewide foster care board rate. Higher amounts need approval from DCF's statewide adoption manager.
legal_citation: s. 409.166, F.S.; Fla. Admin. Code R. 65C-16
notes: Rule detail from Fla. Admin. Code R. 65C-16.0131 summary.

rule_summary: Criminal history screening is verified for the applicant and all household members.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Children over 36 months may not share a bedroom with a child of the opposite gender unless keeping a sibling group together, with listed exceptions. Children may not share with an adult except infants up to 12 months.
notes: 65C-45.005 covers Level I (child-specific) waivable requirements; unclear whether the same wording applies to other levels. An older notice used three years.

rule_summary: Room and board rate for ages 0-5 is $663.03 a month from 1 July 2026 (HB 5301E).
notes: DCF memo, July 2026. Effective 2026-07-01 per memo.

rule_summary: Room and board rate for ages 13-21 is $795.94 a month from 1 July 2026. Older youth also get a supplemental monthly payment of 10 percent of this rate.
notes: Supplemental payment detail from a 2025 memo.

rule_summary: Room and board rate for ages 6-12 is $680.01 a month from 1 July 2026.
notes: DCF memo, July 2026.

rule_summary: An emergency rule notice says a dually licensed foster home may care for no more than five children, including biological, foster and adopted children.
notes: Emergency notice; may not be current. Applies to dually licensed homes; general capacity rule in 409.175(3) not read.

rule_summary: An abuse history check runs through the Florida Safe Families Network for initial licensing.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Each bedroom must have at least two means of exit in an emergency and a smoke alarm in each bedroom area.
notes: value is means of exit. Smoke alarm item may be from another rule in the results.

rule_summary: Initial licensing needs an application and a licensing unified home study. Licensing studies are done by licensed child-placing agencies.
notes: Child-placing agency detail from https://www.myflfamilies.com/services/licensing/foster-care-licensing.

rule_summary: Initial licensing includes proof of income. Applicants should be financially stable.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: An older DCF notice says a licence is valid for no more than one year from issue under s. 409.175.
legal_citation: s. 409.175, F.S.; Fla. Admin. Code R. 65C-45.014
notes: Older notice; may be out of date. Rule 65C-45.014 (terms of a licence) not read.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 21.
notes: Read from search summaries; several secondary sites agree. Regulation text not seen.

rule_summary: Single, married, widowed or divorced people can foster.
notes: Secondary source.

rule_summary: The relicensing file must reach the licensing authority at least 30 days before the licence expires (10 business days under the attestation model). Relicensing may not start more than 90 days before expiry.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be Florida residents. One eligibility list also includes US citizenship.
notes: Citizenship item may come from a secondary site in the same results; unclear. Check the DCF page.

rule_summary: Licensed caregivers must complete continuing education before renewal. A 2020 DCF memo set 8 hours for Level II non-child-specific homes until 65C-45.012 is updated.
legal_citation: s. 409.175, F.S.; Fla. Admin. Code R. 65C-45.012
notes: 2020 memo; may be superseded. Unclear which of the DCF documents in results is the memo.

rule_summary: Pre-service training is required (rule 65C-45.002). PRIDE is named as the state curriculum. A secondary source puts it at 20 to 40 hours, varying by county.
notes: Hours not confirmed from DCF or the rule.

rule_summary: Adoption assistance payments may not exceed the DFCS family foster care per diem the child received just before adoptive placement; a specialised rate exists.
notes: Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Applicants and adult household members need a fingerprint-based national criminal history check before approval, and the standards continue while the home is open.
notes: DFCS policy 14.1 and 14.10. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Children over 3 of different sexes may not share a bedroom; only bedrooms used for sleeping; no child over 1 sleeps in a room with an adult; bedroom must have space for belongings.

notes: Directive is from 2022. Maximum basic rates of $887 (ages 0-11) and $902 (12-20) were reported from a secondary source with no date.

rule_summary: In private agency foster homes an infant may share a bedroom with an adult until the infant is 6 months old.
notes: COMAR 07.05.02 covers private (agency) foster care, not local department resource homes. A Gateway summary says children of opposite sex over 2 may not share a room; source not confirmed.

rule_summary: The monthly board rate set by DHS covers food, housing, utilities and over-the-counter medicine. A one-time initial clothing allowance is paid separately. Trips over 30 miles round trip may be reimbursed.
notes: 2019 guidance. Current dollar amounts not found; a new provider rate structure was reported in 2024.

rule_summary: A resource home cares for no more than six children in foster care.
notes: Snippet was cut off. 2021 directive; COMAR 07.02.25 was rewritten (see SSA/CW #25-02, August 2025) so the rule may have changed. Unclear whether own children count.

rule_summary: All household members aged 18 or over need an initial physical exam and a re-exam at least every 2 years.
notes: Read from search summary; unclear which of the two DHS directives the snippet came from.

rule_summary: Resource family assessment uses the SAFE home study model. The home study visit follows background clearances and pre-service training.
notes: Read from a truncated snippet of SSA/CW #21-09 and the DHS requirements page summary. Nothing recorded from SAFE content.

rule_summary: COMAR 07.02.25 was updated to align with SB708 (2024), the kinship preference law.
notes: Directive SSA/CW #25-02 dated 2025-08-05. Content of the kinship changes not read.

rule_summary: Resource home licences are reconsidered on a cycle set in COMAR 07.02.25; an older table of contents lists an annual reconsideration section. Current term not confirmed.
notes: Chapter was rewritten (proposed repeal of .01-.24 and new .01-.20); section numbers and term may have changed. Unverified.

rule_summary: Resource (foster) and adoptive applicants must be at least 21.
notes: Read from search summary of the DHS requirements page. Unclear whether the page covers adoption as well as fostering.

rule_summary: Applicants give three references on their parenting ability.
notes: Read from search summary. Unit is references.

rule_summary: Resource parents may be married, divorced, widowed or single.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants must be a US citizen or a non-citizen lawfully admitted for permanent residence.
notes: Read from search summary. A Child Welfare Information Gateway summary gives the same rule.

rule_summary: At least 10 hours of training a year, including 2 hours on behaviour management every other year.
notes: Read from a Child Welfare Information Gateway summary, not the regulation.

rule_summary: At least 27 hours of pre-service training before approval. In two-parent homes both must complete it. Most local departments use PRIDE; Baltimore City is reported to use MAPP.
notes: Read from search summary. Curriculum detail came from a secondary source in the same summary and may be out of date.

rule_summary: Adoption subsidy rates are negotiated for each child based on the child's needs and family circumstances, from $0 to $26.25 a day.
notes: Third-party page, undated. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Applicants and adult household members undergo background checks; the FBI check result is needed before final licensing approval.
notes: Policy page dated 2008; household detail from a childwelfare.gov summary. Unclear whether every adult is fingerprinted. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Daily room and board rates by level of care: unlicensed $18.50, Level A $26.25, B $36.75, C $47.25, D $63.00, E $78.75.
notes: From a February 2025 OCFS presentation to the Legislature; unclear whether still current. Rates are daily. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: A specialised children's foster home may not exceed 4 children, including the family's own children under 16, with no more than 2 under age 2; licensed slots may not exceed 3.
notes: Applies to specialised homes (Chapter 15) only; family foster home cap not found. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: No licence is issued until the home passes a fire safety and fire protection inspection; a temporary licence may be issued meanwhile.
notes: Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: The household must have an ongoing, predictable income so the home is kept to the standards in the rules.
notes: 2018 summary. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: The training rule refers to a two-year licensing period; Chapter 16 has a separate Term of License section.
notes: Term inferred from the training rule; text of the Term of License section not seen. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Treatment foster care candidates must be at least 21, may own or rent their home, and may be single, married or partnered.
notes: Applies to treatment foster care only; unclear which source in the search held this text. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 21 years old.
notes: 2018 childwelfare.gov summary citing Chapter 16; not confirmed in current rule text. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: The licensee must report any changes in the foster home to the licensing worker or supervisor within five days.
notes: Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: An applicant must live in Maine and intend to live in Maine for the licensing period.
notes: Justia copy current through March 2024. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Licensees complete at least 18 combined hours of training in each two-year licensing period, at least 6 by a secondary foster parent if there is one.
notes: 2018 summary; the 18 hours is per two-year licence period, not per year. May be out of date. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: Applicants complete an application, a home study and training, including the Resource Family Introductory Training (RFIT) run for OCFS by the University of Southern Maine.
notes: Policy page dated 2008. RFIT hours per applicant not found. Read from search result summary; page not opened.

rule_summary: The daily standard foster care rate is the base for the adoption assistance maximum daily rate. Higher amounts need an approved difficulty of care assessment.
notes: Read from search summary of AAM 210, effective 2025-01-01. Medicaid and non-recurring costs not seen.

rule_summary: No foster family home licence may be issued or renewed without a criminal history check. The applicant rule also includes a central registry check.
notes: Read from a truncated 2018 statute excerpt. Fingerprinting and which household members are checked not confirmed.

rule_summary: Bedrooms must have enough space for occupants and beds, with head clearance for each child. Halls, closets, stairways, garages, sheds and outbuildings are not bedrooms. No video cameras in bedrooms of foster children over 2.
notes: Read from search summary; compliance record CWL-3080 lists the same limits. Rules on sharing by age or sex not found.

rule_summary: MDHHS pays daily maintenance rates every two weeks; the rate rises automatically on the child's 13th birthday. Difficulty of care payments may be added. A 2023 release put monthly amounts at about $670 (to age 12) and $800 (13 and over).
notes: Dollar figures from a 2023 governor's press release; current FOM 905-3 table not seen. No single value recorded.

rule_summary: A foster family home cares for 1 to 4 children. A foster family group home cares for 5 or 6.
notes: Read from labels on the licensing compliance record form (CWL-3080, rev. 7-23), not the rule text. Statutory definition not confirmed.

rule_summary: Any adult household member who cares for foster children must meet the same qualifications as the applicant, including health.
notes: Read from an older (2015) edition of the rules in search results; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Since 1 January 2023 the department issues an extended licence to a foster family home licensed for at least one year and in good standing.
notes: Read from search summary; exact source of the extended-licence text unclear (rule file or statute). Length of initial and extended licence not found.

rule_summary: Foster home applicants and licensees must be 18 or older, in sound physical, mental and emotional health, and willing to accept a foster child as a household member.
notes: Read from search summary. Amended 2023, effective 2023-06-16. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: The agency gives the licensee a renewal application at least 60 calendar days before the licence expires.
notes: Read from search summary; unclear whether this rule is in the foster home rules or the child placing agency rules.

rule_summary: After the initial period each licensee completes at least 6 hours of training a year under the agency's training plan.
notes: Read from search summary. An older version required 12 further hours over the first 2 years before the annual 6.

rule_summary: Applicants attend orientation before applying. Each person named on the licence completes at least 12 hours of training before licensure can be recommended; the state GROW course is about 20 to 25 hours.
notes: Read from search summary. A news source gives 30 hours, which does not match official sources.

rule_summary: Northstar adoption assistance includes medical assistance, a basic payment and possible difficulty of care payment. Children who reach permanency before age 6 get 50 percent of the foster care rate they would otherwise get.
notes: Read from search summary of 2025 statute and a Families Rising page. Dollar amounts on the Families Rising page carry no year.

rule_summary: The licence holder and other people named in Minnesota Statutes, including roomers or boarders, must have a background study.
notes: Read from search summary (current through Register 2024-09-23). Fingerprinting and age of household members checked not confirmed.

rule_summary: Foster children may share a bedroom with a same-sex child if the room is large enough, but not with an adult or a child of the opposite sex.
notes: Read from a county requirements page, not the rule. Rule text (2960.3040, physical environment) not seen; exceptions such as for infants not confirmed.

rule_summary: Under Northstar Care for Children, foster, adoptive and relative custodian families get a basic monthly payment by age, plus possible difficulty of care payments. 2023-24 basic rates were $731 (0-5), $866 (6-12), $1,023 (13-20).
notes: Rates for 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30 from a county rate sheet; current rates not found. Statute says yearly increases may not exceed 3 percent.

rule_summary: A foster home may care for no more than six foster children and no more than eight children in total, including the foster family's own children.
notes: Read from search summary; summary said 'one version', so the current text and any variance rules are not confirmed.

rule_summary: The licensing agency decides whether the prospective licence holder can provide appropriate structure and is suitable to be licensed.
notes: Read from search summary. Home study model not named in results.

rule_summary: Licences issued by counties under this section may run for up to two years. A 2024 law moves family child foster care to continuous licences renewed automatically each year once licensing moves to DCYF.
notes: Read from search summary. Unclear whether the continuous licensing change is in effect yet (transfer was planned for July 2025). Statewide rule; counties license homes.

rule_summary: Foster care licence applicants must be at least 21 at the time of application.
notes: Read from search summary of a DHS document. Statewide rule; licensing is run by counties and licensed private agencies, which may add requirements. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: County pages say applicants apply through the county where they live.
notes: County practice, not confirmed as a statewide rule.

rule_summary: Licensed foster parents complete 12 hours of training a year to keep the licence active.
notes: Read from county pages in search results, not the rule. Dakota County says 2 of the 12 hours must be on mental health; unclear whether that is statewide.

rule_summary: Non-relative applicants finish pre-service training before licensing, including at least 6 hours of orientation, reasonable and prudent parenting training and 2 hours of children's mental health training.
notes: Read from a Child Welfare Information Gateway summary (which cites 2960.3060). Counties may require more.

rule_summary: Qualifying children get a basic subsidy package: maintenance, child care, respite, reimbursement of non-recurring adoption costs, and Medicaid. SFY 2024 monthly rates were $368 (0-5), $435 (6-12), $571 (13+).
notes: From a third-party state profile and a DSS bulletin in search results. May be out of date.

rule_summary: Applicants and household members aged 17 and over are fingerprinted and background-screened. SB71 raised this age to 18; a proposed and an emergency rule follow that change.
notes: Sources disagree because of the SB71 change; unclear whether the age is now 18 in the final rule. Unit refers to age of household members checked.

rule_summary: Rules cover where sleeping rooms are located and drawer and closet space. No foster youth may sleep in the same room as an adult aged 21 or over.
notes: Read from a 2016 memo and a DSS notice in search results. Cornell lists a version effective 2026-02-11; whether these provisions changed is not confirmed.

rule_summary: State fiscal year 2024 monthly foster care rates were $345 (ages 0-5), $408 (6-12) and $455 (13 and over), plus a $91 monthly infant allowance.
notes: Rates labelled SFY 2024 (and 'unlicensed' in the summary); current licensed rates not confirmed. A newer memo (cd24-23) may update them.

rule_summary: No more than six children in a foster home. No more than two under age 2 and four under age 5, except temporarily for a sibling group. Homes caring for youth with elevated needs are limited to four placements.
notes: Read from search summary of current text. A 2016 memo described a maximum of five, so older and newer sources differ.

rule_summary: Applicants complete a child abuse and neglect check.
notes: Read from search summary of a state flyer.

rule_summary: Household members need physician statements and up-to-date immunisations.
notes: Read from a 2016 memo; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Licensure follows STARS training, online trainings and in-home assessments (the resource provider family assessment).
notes: Read from search summary. Model not named.

rule_summary: Applicants must be employed or have adequate income.
notes: From a 2017 foster-adopt association packet, not an official source.

rule_summary: A foster home licence is valid for 2 years before renewal.
notes: From an ICPC state summary, not the rule.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 21.
notes: Age read from a 2016 DSS memo summarising the rule and a state flyer; rule version effective 2024-04-30 not read in full. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: At least 30 hours of in-service training are needed to renew a licence.
notes: Figure from a December 2018 Children's Division memo cited in search summary; the manual section on in-service training is the URL given. May be out of date.

rule_summary: Pre-service training is STARS (Specialized Training, Assessment, Resources, Support and Skills), plus CPR and first aid, a secondhand smoke module and HIPAA training.
notes: Read from search summary. Total hours not found.

rule_summary: Adoption subsidy is based on the child's special needs, not family income, and may not exceed the foster care board rate. Payments start after finalisation and usually end at 18.
legal_citation: 18 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 6, Ch. 1, Subpt. G
notes: Read from search summary; payment timing came from a third-party state profile. An older table of basic rates ($325 to $400 by age) is probably out of date.

rule_summary: Applicants must pass a criminal background check. Household members aged 14 and older are checked.
notes: Read from search summary. Part 7 governs agencies' resource home services; a 2018 summary gives the same age. Unit refers to the age from which household members are checked.

rule_summary: Each foster child has their own age-appropriate bed. No more than four same-sex children per bedroom, and children over 3 may not share with a child of the opposite sex. No adult may share a child's room.
notes: From a 2018 summary citing an older rule number; the ICPC summary is less specific. May be out of date.

rule_summary: From 1 January 2026 the monthly board rate is $669.88 (ages 0-8), $768.05 (9-15) and $847.21 (16-21), plus clothing and personal allowances.
notes: Read from search summary of the MDCPS 2026 schedule. Several rates, so no single value recorded.

rule_summary: Limits on total children in the home differ by source: an ICPC summary gives a total of 5 children; an MDCPS page is reported as no more than six (foster, adopted or birth).
notes: Sources disagree; news articles give four or five. Rule text not seen. No value recorded.

rule_summary: A resource home must be well heated or cooled, well ventilated and have a working telephone.
legal_citation: 18 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 6, Ch. 1, Subpt. F
notes: Read from search summary; exact subsection not confirmed.

rule_summary: Applicants must be financially self-supporting. No income figure was stated.
notes: Same caveat on URL as the residency row.

rule_summary: Resource (foster) applicants must be at least 21.
notes: From a February 2018 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary; an MDCPS foster care page in search results also says 21. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: MDCPS licensure policy includes a licence re-evaluation section. Term and content not seen.
notes: Only a table of contents entry was seen (policy revised 2020-01-27).

rule_summary: Applicants must be legal Mississippi residents.
notes: Read from search summary of an MDCPS page; unclear whether the summary came from this URL or the MDCPS Foster Care Policy PDF.

rule_summary: Caretakers complete 10 hours of in-service training a year; no more than 5 of these may be home-based or online modules.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: All caretakers complete 27 hours of pre-service training, including Mississippi PATH (15 hours), blood-borne pathogens, car seat safety, and first aid and CPR.
notes: Read from search summary. Part 7 (licensed agencies) sets 24 hours, which may apply to private agency homes instead.

rule_summary: Adoption assistance basic rates are $20.73 a day (0-12) and $24.49 (13+), with higher specialised rates; the maximum is not guaranteed. Assistance and Medicaid end at 18.
notes: From an undated third-party state profile; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Applicants have background checks; certain serious convictions prevent licensing.
notes: Read from search summary. Which household members are checked not confirmed.

rule_summary: Sleeping arrangements are set in ARM 37.51.816. Sleeping areas used by foster children must have two unobstructed exits.
notes: Rule text not seen. Exit rule came from the DPHHS fire safety checklist. Manual is UNPAM-108, revised 03/2025.

rule_summary: Family and kinship foster care is paid at one daily rate for all ages: $32.30 a day from 1 July 2025 and $33.27 from 1 July 2026. Therapeutic foster care is paid at a higher rate.
notes: Read from search summary of the DPHHS rate matrix. A 2025 legislative fact sheet showed $31.36 for SFY 2025. Daily rate, so no monthly value.

rule_summary: A youth foster home cares for at most six children or youth, not counting the foster parents' own children, stepchildren or wards. A 2024 rule change proposed allowing exceptions.
notes: Read from search summary. Unclear whether the 2024 amendment (MAR 37-1004) was adopted as proposed.

rule_summary: Home ownership is not required; applicants may rent or own a house or apartment if the home meets health and safety standards.
notes: Read from search summary of a DPHHS FAQ and AdoptUSKids. Landlord consent not mentioned.

rule_summary: The initial youth foster or kinship home licence is for one year; the department may then renew it every two years.
notes: Read from a 2024 proposal in tracked changes; adopted text (this URL is the adoption notice) not confirmed. No value recorded because two terms apply.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 18.
notes: Read from search summary; a 2018 Gateway summary gives the same. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: Foster parents document required training when relicensed. A news report says 15 hours a year.
notes: Hours from a news report only; rule hours not seen.

rule_summary: Applicants must finish free Resource Parent Training before licensing. A news report puts it at 18 hours.
notes: Hours came from a news report, not DPHHS, so no value recorded.

rule_summary: Applicants and adult household members must have state and national fingerprint-based criminal history checks. Refusing consent is grounds to bar a person from providing foster care.
notes: Fingerprint process updated from 2 December 2024 according to an NCDHHS letter. Age threshold for household checks not confirmed.

rule_summary: No more than four children may share a bedroom. A child under six may not share with a child over 12 unless they are siblings placed together.
notes: Room sharing text read from a third-party mirror summary; not confirmed on the official OAH copy.

rule_summary: Standard monthly board rates, unchanged since 1 July 2023: 702 dollars (age 0-5), 742 (6-12), 810 (13 and over). These standard rates also apply to adoption assistance.
notes: An NCDHHS memo says rates had not risen as of 30 June 2026. Applies_to both because the memo groups foster care and adoption; unverified. Value blank as rates vary by age.

rule_summary: No more than five children may live in a family foster home at one time, counting the foster parents' own children and any children cared for as babysitting or day care. Waivers are possible, mainly to place siblings together.
notes: Household members 18 and over not in care are not counted. Subchapter 70E was under periodic review in 2025-2026; text may change.

rule_summary: Applicants may own or rent a home, trailer or apartment.
notes: Read from search summary. Landlord consent rule not seen.

rule_summary: Unlicensed kinship carers may receive about half the board rate: 351 dollars a month (age 0-5), 371 (6-12) and 405 (13 and over).
notes: Read from search summary; unclear which NCDHHS document gave these figures.

rule_summary: Not confirmed. The 20-hours-before-renewal rule and 10 hours a year point to a two-year licence, but no snippet stated the term.
notes: Inference only; unverified. Kept so the gap is visible.

rule_summary: The state minimum age to adopt is 18. Some county agencies (for example Mecklenburg and Forsyth) state 21.
notes: Sources differ between state (18) and some county pages (21).

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 21.
notes: Read from NCDHHS summary; regulation section not seen. North Carolina is county-administered; county DSS agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Applicants may be single, married, divorced or widowed.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Each foster parent must complete 20 hours of in-service training before licence renewal. The supervising agency must offer 10 hours a year.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: All prospective resource parents must complete 30 hours of pre-service training. TIPS-MAPP or an equivalent is the usual curriculum.
notes: 30-hour rule seen in NCDHHS documents; curriculum named on county pages. Mecklenburg page used as source; state document URL unclear from snippet.

rule_summary: Licensing requires an initial background check and an initial and annual child abuse and neglect index check.
notes: Read from search summary. Who in the household is checked not seen.

rule_summary: Children in care must have adequate space for belongings and privacy in their bedroom. Temporary bed space (such as an air mattress) is limited to 14 calendar days. A worksheet asks for detail if more than two children share a room.
notes: Read from policy manual summary, not the rule. Bedroom-sharing limit not confirmed.

rule_summary: Monthly family foster care maintenance rates are set by child age. The July 2023 schedule gave 840 dollars (age 0-4) and 960 dollars (5-12). A new schedule took effect 1 July 2025.
notes: 2025 amounts not visible in the snippet; the 2023 figures are out of date. Rate for 13 and over not seen.

rule_summary: A full family foster home licence is described as care for up to six children.
notes: Read from a 2022 newspaper summary, not the rule text. Unclear whether the six includes the carer's own children.

rule_summary: A foster home may be a dwelling, mobile home, housing unit or apartment occupied by one person or a single family. The home must meet fire code and zoning rules.
notes: Read from search summary. Renting not addressed directly.

rule_summary: Identified relatives can be licensed under a separate section of the rule, with lower renewal training hours (8 per period) and an abbreviated PRIDE option.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Licences are renewed every two years. A renewal notice is sent 90 days before expiry.
notes: Two-year renewal period read from SFN 1037 summary.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 21, single or married.
notes: Also stated in DHS licensing manual 622-05. Local human service zones deliver services; they may have local practice but licensing standards are statewide.

rule_summary: Applicants may be single or married.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Before initial licensure and each renewal, each foster parent must complete a fire prevention and safety course.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Each applicant on a full licence must complete at least 16 hours of training each two-year renewal period (8 hours for certified or relative homes).
notes: From licensing packet SFN 1037 (March 2025). The policy manual (2023) says 13 hours each licensing period; an older version said 13 hours a year. Sources disagree.

rule_summary: Prospective foster parents must complete orientation and the state pre-service training (UNITY or PRIDE) before placement, or within the first year if approved. An abbreviated 3-hour PRIDE option exists for relatives.
notes: Abbreviated PRIDE created April 2024. Hours of full pre-service training not found.

rule_summary: The monthly adoption assistance amount is set using the Nebraska Caregiver Responsibilities (NCR) tool. Families may ask to change the agreement at any time. The child generally must be a state ward when the petition is filed.
notes: From a third-party state profile updated May 2025.

rule_summary: Household members aged 18 and over are checked, including a fingerprint-based FBI national criminal history check.
notes: Read from search summary. A contracted agency says household members over 13 are checked; sources disagree. Unit refers to age of household members checked.

rule_summary: The rules set standards for bedrooms or sleeping areas. Every level used for sleeping needs at least two means of escape and working smoke detectors.
notes: Bedroom criteria cut off in snippet. Escape and smoke detector rule from a 2018 Gateway summary.

rule_summary: DHHS publishes foster care rates by fiscal year and age band (0-5, 6-11, 12-18). 2019 monthly base rates were about $620.50, $713.58 and $775.63. A 2 percent rise was applied in 2023-24.
notes: Current base rates not confirmed; 2019 figures came from a Children's Commission fact sheet. The rate committee is due to end on 2026-07-01 under LB346.

rule_summary: The licence states the number and ages of children the home may care for. Total placement limits are set in 395 NAC 3-003.06; a 2020 draft proposed six children with two foster parents and four with one.
notes: Final limits not confirmed; the six/four figures come from a 2020 DHHS draft. Justia copy current through 2024-09-17.

rule_summary: Licensing needs pre-service training, an application, background checks and a home study.
notes: From a contracted agency page. Model not named.

rule_summary: Applicants need employment or a reliable income source and must meet basic income guidelines.
notes: From a contracted agency's FAQ. No figure given.

rule_summary: A foster care licence is effective for two years.
notes: Read from search summary; Justia copy current through 2024-09-17.

rule_summary: Foster parent applicants must be at least 21.
notes: From a contracted agency's FAQ, not DHHS. A 2019 DHHS draft rule states an age but the figure was cut off in the snippet. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: Married and single applicants, with or without children, and those living in a house or apartment are accepted.
notes: From a contracted agency's FAQ; the same page also says LGBTQIA+ applicants are accepted. Renting rules and landlord consent not found.

rule_summary: Licence renewal needs at least 12 clock-hours of approved in-service training a year. Statute bars renewal without the training hours set by the department.
notes: From a 2018 Gateway summary and an older statute version; current figure not confirmed.

rule_summary: Pre-service training is required for all foster parents. Agencies describe TIPS-MAPP (10 weeks) and, more recently, the NTDC curriculum (8 weekly sessions).
notes: From contracted agency pages; curriculum may have changed from TIPS-MAPP to NTDC. Hours not found.

rule_summary: Applicants complete 21 clock-hours of pre-service training within the 12 months before licensing and give written proof.
notes: From a February 2018 Gateway summary; may be out of date, as DHHS proposed training changes in 2019 and 2020.

rule_summary: Applicants need a valid driving licence and/or reliable transport.
notes: From a contracted agency's FAQ.

rule_summary: Adoption subsidies can include one-time payments for costs not covered by insurance or Medicaid. Non-recurring costs such as fees are reimbursed if the child meets the special needs definition. Payments may begin at placement.
notes: Read from search summary, combined with DCYF Policy 1802 and an April 2025 Gateway profile. Monthly amount not found.

rule_summary: Applicants and household members aged 18 or over have an FBI fingerprint check and a sex offender registry review; those who lived outside the state in the past 5 years also get out-of-state checks.
notes: Read from search summary. Unit refers to age of household members checked.

rule_summary: Each child in care over age 1 needs a bedroom separate from adults, and separate from children of the opposite sex over age 5.
notes: From a 2018 Gateway summary; current He-C 6446.09 text not seen and may differ.

rule_summary: From 1 July 2024 general foster care is paid daily at $34.28 (ages 0-5), $38.51 (6-11) and $40.78 (12-17). Specialised, emergency and crisis care are paid at higher rates.
notes: Read from search summary of the DHHS page. Daily rates by age, so no single value recorded. A 2025 update not confirmed.

rule_summary: A home with 2 licensed foster parents may care for no more than 6 children under 21; a home with 1 licensed parent no more than 4. Statute caps unrelated children at 6, with a sibling exception.
notes: Read from search summary of Justia copy current through 2025-03-27. Exact RSA 170-E section not confirmed. Value is the two-parent limit.

rule_summary: Household members aged 18 or over who lived outside New Hampshire in the past 5 years need out-of-state child abuse registry checks.
notes: Read from search summary. In-state registry check not described in the snippet.

rule_summary: Homes must be inspected. The physical environment rule requires barrier-free access for children with physical or medical needs and basic first-aid supplies.
notes: Read from search summary; snippet showed only part of the section.

rule_summary: All prospective adoptive families must be licensed as foster families by DCYF.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A permit for family foster care is valid for up to 6 months from issue. A 2024 bill (HB 1573) created a separate kinship care home licence.
notes: Read from search summary. Status of HB 1573 not confirmed. Full licence term not found.

rule_summary: New Hampshire residents aged 21 or older may apply to be licensed foster parents.
notes: From a resource page summarising DCYF; rule section for age not seen. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: Renewal involves a home visit, a written assessment of compliance, and criminal records and local police checks on the foster parent and household members aged 18 or over.
notes: Read from search summary (current through Register 2024-10-03). Licence length not found.

rule_summary: Applicants must be New Hampshire residents.
notes: From a resource page; not confirmed in the rule.

rule_summary: Pre-licensing training totals at least 30 hours, in units of at least 1 hour. Applicants licensed in New Hampshire in the past 4 years may be exempt from unchanged topics.
notes: Exact section not shown in the snippet. UNH's DCYF pre-service course is listed as 23 hours, so sources differ.

rule_summary: A 2015 DCP&P schedule set monthly adoption assistance by age: 763 dollars (0-5), 845 (6-9), 872 (10-12), 907 (13 and over).
notes: Figures effective 1 January 2015 from a non-state page; likely out of date. Value left blank as rates vary by age.

rule_summary: Applicants and each household member aged 18 or over, including boarders and frequent overnight guests, must complete state and federal criminal history checks, including members who turn 18.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A child's sleeping room must be large enough for the child's safety, privacy and comfort. Further bedroom and sharing rules are in 3A:51-4.2 and 4.3.
notes: Read from search summary. Bedroom sharing details (3A:51-4.3) not seen.

rule_summary: Resource families receive a monthly board payment, a clothing allowance and health care coverage for the child.
notes: Current amounts not found. Statute 30:4C-27.2 provides for a clothing component in the monthly allowance.

rule_summary: No more than four children in placement and six children in total in the home, no more than four under age six and two under age two, and no more than two non-ambulatory children.
notes: Limits apply to placements on or after 6 February 2006. Four-in-placement limit also applies. Licensing may exceed limits to keep siblings together, or set lower limits.

rule_summary: New Jersey uses the SAFE home study format for resource family and adoptive homes.
notes: Read from a secondary summary page, not a state source.

rule_summary: Relatives and family friends take Traditions of Caring training instead of PRIDE. A 2025 proposal would move kinship standards into a new chapter 3A:51A.
notes: Proposal notice 57 N.J.R. 1750; unclear whether it has been adopted.

rule_summary: Each resource family licensing period is three years. The licence must be kept in the home, and the home is inspected annually.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants for an initial resource family licence must be at least 18 and live in New Jersey. Resource family licensing covers foster and adoptive homes.
notes: Read from search summary of the general personal requirements section. Chapter 51 copy shows an expiry date of 5 July 2026; unclear whether it has been readopted.

rule_summary: Applicants submit references under 3A:51-5.2, and references are also required for each new household member.
notes: Number of references not seen in the snippet.

rule_summary: An applicant for an initial resource family licence must be a resident of New Jersey.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Each resource family parent must complete annual in-service training provided or approved by the Department.
notes: Number of hours not seen in the snippet.

rule_summary: Each primary and secondary applicant must complete PRIDE pre-service training. Relatives and family friends take Traditions of Caring training instead.
notes: PRIDE requirement read from the regulation summary. The 27-hour figure came from a secondary source (AdoptUsKids state page), not the regulation; unverified.

rule_summary: Criminal records checks, including fingerprints, are required for foster care provider licensure, with abuse and neglect screening for all adults in the home.
notes: Details of who is checked read from the CYFD renewal summary; unverified.

rule_summary: Foster parents and other adults need a separate bedroom (infants under 18 months excepted). Each foster child needs their own bed. Children over 5 generally do not share with an unrelated child of the opposite gender.
notes: Read from a 2018 summary that predates the 2020 replacement rule; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Monthly maintenance payments vary by age and level of care. A summary lists basic rates of about 627 to 689 dollars a month by age band. A temporary 125 dollar monthly rise was funded from 1 July 2025.
notes: Rate table on ICPC page is undated and its unit label is ambiguous (per day vs per month). Increase reported in a June 2025 legislative handout.

rule_summary: No more than eight children in total in the home, of whom no more than six may be in foster care. Lower limits may be set after the home study; the regional manager may approve more.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: New Mexico uses the SAFE home study, which is updated at renewal.
notes: Read from search summary of a CYFD renewal page; unclear which CYFD URL holds this text.

rule_summary: Foster care licences must be renewed every two years, with an updated home study, background checks and training hours.
notes: Read from search summary; unclear which of several CYFD short URLs carries the renewal page.

rule_summary: Any adult aged 18 or over who lives in New Mexico can apply to be licensed as a foster care provider. The rule covers foster and adoptive homes.
notes: Age seen in an older version and in a 2019 emergency amendment; unclear whether the current text (rule replaced effective 11 February 2020) keeps the same wording.

rule_summary: A licence will not be issued to an applicant whose own children are currently in foster care. Applicants whose parental rights were terminated or relinquished are considered case by case.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Citizenship or immigration status does not prevent eligibility for licensure. Separate guidance covers non-US citizens without legal permanent residency.
notes: Read from search summary. Older text required legal US residency; current text appears to have dropped this.

rule_summary: Foster care providers must complete at least 12 hours of approved training each year.
notes: From the 2019 amendment; may have changed in the 2020 replacement rule.

rule_summary: All applicants must complete pre-service training before licensing, and household members aged 17 and over must attend. CYFD uses the READi NM pre-service curriculum.
notes: From the 2019 amendment; READi name from a CYFD page. Number of hours not found.

rule_summary: The monthly adoption assistance rate may be negotiated up to, but not above, the family foster care rate. Special rate and medically fragile add-ons exist. Payments end at 18, or 19 if in school.
notes: DCFS policy dated June 2024. A 2024 DCFS page lists a cap of $682.94 / $773.17, lower than the 2023 foster rates; sources disagree.

rule_summary: Applicants are fingerprinted. Clark County says any felony conviction may stop an application before fingerprinting and training.
notes: Clark County page, not a statewide rule. Which household members are checked not confirmed. Statewide rule. Clark and Washoe counties run their own child welfare and licensing and may add requirements.

rule_summary: From 1 July 2023 DCFS family and relative foster care is $858.02 a month (ages 0-12) and $971.38 (13 and over). Advanced and specialised foster care are paid at higher rates.
notes: DCFS rate sheet; may have been updated since 2023. Two age bands, so no single value recorded. Clark and Washoe may pay different rates.

rule_summary: A licensing representative sets each home's total capacity based on the foster parents' own children under 16 and the home's space. No more than two children under 18 months or four under 5 without approval, counting own children.
notes: Read from a mirror current through 2024-12-31. No fixed family home maximum seen; group foster homes are capped at 15. A 1999 proposal set six; not current.

rule_summary: After training, applicants complete a background check and a home study. DCFS inspects each home at initial licensing and at least once a year after.
notes: Read from search summary and a 2024 DHHS release on rural training. Model not named.

rule_summary: Applicants do not have to own their home to foster.
notes: Read from search summary. Clark County also asks for proof of homeowner's or renter's insurance. Statewide rule. Clark and Washoe counties run their own child welfare and licensing and may add requirements.

rule_summary: The licensing authority must ensure a foster home is financially solvent.
notes: Read from search summary. No figure given.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be 21 or older.
notes: Read from search summary. Statewide rule. Clark and Washoe counties run their own child welfare and licensing and may add requirements. Adoption minimum age not found.

rule_summary: Clark County estimates at least 3 months from pre-screen to full licence.
notes: Clark County estimate only; not statewide.

rule_summary: Primary caregivers complete 27 hours of pre-service training, provided free by the agency.
notes: Sources disagree: Clark County says 24 hours, AdoptUSKids about 30, and an older code version at least 8. Statewide rule. Clark and Washoe counties run their own child welfare and licensing and may add requirements.

rule_summary: Criminal history checks are required for prospective foster and adoptive parents and anyone over 18 living in the home. Fingerprints for state and federal checks are due within two weeks of placement.
notes: Read from search summary. Certain convictions require denial (443.8(e)). Further checks at renewal (443.10).

rule_summary: Physical plant standards are in 18 NYCRR 443.3. County pages say a bed is needed for each child and that children can share a bedroom.
notes: Bedroom text of 443.3 not seen; bed and sharing points from Dutchess and Schenectady county pages.

rule_summary: OCFS sets maximum state aid rates for foster boarding home payments, published on its rates pages. A bill (A00718) would add cost-of-living adjustments to these base rates.
notes: Current rate amounts not found. Bill status: in committee as of January 2026.

rule_summary: A foster family boarding home may care for no more than six children, counting all children in the home. The limit may be exceeded only to take back a child returning to that home.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Unless the agency permits otherwise, no more than two infants under two years of age, including the foster parents' own children.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A county page says applicants must have their own source of income.
notes: County page only; no state rule seen.

rule_summary: NYC ACS materials give a minimum age of 18 to adopt. OCFS states that you do not need to be a foster parent to adopt.
notes: Age 18 read from an ACS brochure summary, not from state regulation. Unclear whether this is a statewide rule.

rule_summary: Each foster parent must be at least 21.
notes: Read from a 2018 federal summary of 18 NYCRR 443.2; not checked against the current regulation. New York is county-administered; local districts and voluntary agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: County pages state that applicants may be married, single or living in a partnership.
notes: Read from county pages (Ulster, Dutchess), not a state source.

rule_summary: Certificates are renewed under 18 NYCRR 443.10, which may require new state and national checks for adults who joined the home or turned 18 since the last certification.
notes: Certificate term not seen in a snippet; a summary mentioned annual renewal but this is unverified.

rule_summary: A county page says each certified foster parent must complete at least four hours of further training a year.
notes: From Erie County page; not confirmed in state regulation.

rule_summary: Pre-certification training is required. NYC replaced MAPP with the NTDC curriculum in January 2025. County pages describe about 30 hours over ten weeks.
notes: 30 hours from a county page (Sullivan); state regulation hours not found. Curriculum may differ by district or agency.

rule_summary: All adults in the home must pass a background check. Rule 5101:2-7-02 has an appendix of disqualifying offences.
notes: Read from secondary summary; check rule detail not seen.

rule_summary: A bedroom for foster children holds no more than four children. A foster child may not share with a child of the opposite sex unless all are under five. Individual bedrooms are not required.
notes: Four-per-room figure from a 2018 summary; capacity exceptions were later amended, so may have changed.

rule_summary: A foster home may have no more than five foster children. Caregivers certified under two years (or with under two years of child care experience) may have no more than three.
