notes: Read from search summary. Unclear whether the caregiver's own children count toward five; an older version set a total of ten children under supervision.

rule_summary: No more than two children under age two and no more than four under age five may live in or receive child care in the home.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: An initial application leads to a foster care homestudy completed by the recommending agency.
notes: Model not named in snippets.

rule_summary: Applicants may rent or own. One agency says renters need adequate space and the landlord's approval to care for foster children.
notes: Landlord approval point is from a private agency page; unclear whether it is a state rule.

rule_summary: An applicant must be at least 18 at initial certification as a foster caregiver.
notes: An amendment replaced 21 with 18; a 2018 federal summary still says 21 and appears out of date. Ohio is county-administered; public children services agencies and private agencies may set further requirements.

rule_summary: A foster caregiver or applicant may be a legally married couple, a single person or co-parents.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Some agencies describe licensing as generally taking 45 to 60 days from the start of the process.
notes: Private agency page, not a state rule.

rule_summary: Family foster caregivers must complete at least 30 hours of continuing training in each certification period.
notes: Reduced from 40 hours in 2021. Older sources still show 40 hours over two years.

rule_summary: Family foster caregivers must complete at least 24 hours of preplacement training before the agency recommends certification. Up to 36 hours can be reimbursed.
notes: Figure read from tracked-changes text of a 2021 amendment; older sources say 36 hours. Final wording not confirmed.

rule_summary: Background investigations are done at application under OAC 340:75-7-15. Annual updates include a re-issue of fingerprint results and a RAP Back check.
notes: Detail of who is checked not seen.

rule_summary: Preferably no more than two children share a bedroom, with related children considered first by age and emotional needs.
notes: Justia copy current through September 2024; may predate the 2025 version.

rule_summary: OKDHS pays a monthly foster care reimbursement. Its rates page lists a resource parent rate of 43.86 dollars, unit unclear.
notes: Page layout in snippet was garbled; unclear whether 43.86 is a daily rate or another category.

rule_summary: The total number of children in OKDHS custody placed in a resource home does not exceed five. OKDHS sets the number and ages of children for each home.
notes: From the version effective until 14 September 2025; current version not seen.

rule_summary: Applicants complete a Resource Family Assessment (RFA).
notes: Model behind the RFA not named in snippets.

rule_summary: A contracted agency states that applicants must own or rent a house or apartment.
notes: No OKDHS statement on renting found.

rule_summary: Kinship resource homes, paid or unpaid, must meet the same requirements as traditional non-related homes. Case-by-case exceptions are allowed for some non-safety requirements.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: All foster (resource) family applicants must be at least 21.
notes: Citation from a federal summary; the rule has a version effective 14 September 2025 that was not seen.

rule_summary: Foster parents may be married, single, or family members with a stable living arrangement.
notes: This rule covers foster homes supervised by private foster home agencies; OKDHS page states the same for its homes.

rule_summary: Applicants must be residing lawfully in the United States.
notes: Read from a 2018 federal summary; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Each resource parent completes 12 hours of continuing in-service training each year. OKDHS provides free options.
notes: Version effective 14 September 2025.

rule_summary: An OKDHS FAQ says foster parents complete 27 hours of pre-service training, including 6 hours of behaviour crisis management, before approval.
notes: A federal case study says kinship training was reduced from 27 to 12 hours. Hours in the September 2025 rule not seen.

rule_summary: Monthly base rate: 693 dollars (age 0-5), 733 (6-12), 795 (13-20). Payments vary by age and level of need.
notes: From a 2025 legislative committee document, which says direct payments had not changed since the 2018 increase. Value blank as rates vary by age.

rule_summary: A single-parent household can have up to four children, including children already living in the home. No more than two children under age three. All children living in the home are counted.
notes: Four-child single-parent figure read from ODHS FAQ summary; two-parent cap not seen. The Department may approve an extra child in special circumstances.

rule_summary: Resource parents may live in a house or apartment but must have a room for the child. The home must be the family's primary residence.
notes: Apartment point read from an ODHS-linked guide; primary residence rule from OAR 413-200-0335.

rule_summary: Resource parents need a source of income or financial resources to support themselves and their family.
notes: A 211info listing says families cannot depend on the foster care payment.

rule_summary: Relative caregivers are certified under the same criteria as foster parents, with an age exception for relatives aged 18 to 20.
notes: From a 2019 training deck; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Certificates of Approval run for a two-year certification period.
notes: Inferred from the two-year training period on the renewal page; rule section not seen.

rule_summary: A newly certified applicant must be at least 21. A program manager may approve a relative caregiver aged 18 to 20 as an exception. The rules also cover approval of potential adoptive resources.
notes: Read from a 2018 federal summary; rules have since been renumbered. ODHS FAQ also states 21.

rule_summary: Single people, couples, and people who are married, divorced, widowed or in a domestic partnership can be resource parents.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Certified non-relative resource parents need 30 hours of training in each two-year certification period. RAFT counts toward the first period.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Certification requires the RAFT course (nine 3-hour sessions, 27 hours) and a 2-hour on-demand orientation.
notes: Orientation from the 2026 ODHS training catalogue.

rule_summary: Act 160 of 2004 requires criminal, FBI and child abuse checks on applicants and adults in the home, and a resource family registry for all foster and adoptive applicants. Clearances are renewed every 24 months.
notes: Sources disagree on the age threshold for household checks (14 or 18).

rule_summary: Foster children of the opposite sex aged 5 or older may not share a bedroom. Home standards are in 55 Pa. Code 3700.66 and 3700.67.
notes: From a 2018 federal summary. A commercial blog cites a four-per-room limit, but that figure is from the residential facility rules (3800.102), not Chapter 3700.

rule_summary: Agencies must limit the number of children living with a foster family to six, including the foster parents' own children.
notes: Read from a county-hosted copy of Chapter 3700; not checked against the official Pa. Code.

rule_summary: Financial stability is considered as part of home approval. Sources disagree on whether a set income level is required.
notes: Secondary sources only; no state rule seen.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 21.
notes: DHS foster care page states the same. Pennsylvania is county-administered; county children and youth agencies and private foster family care agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Single people and two-parent families may foster.
notes: Read from private agency pages, not a state source.

rule_summary: Foster parents must complete 3 hours of training on recognising and reporting child abuse within 90 days of approval, then 3 hours every five years.
notes: Read from search summary (Justia copy of 2023 statutes).

rule_summary: Each foster parent must take part in at least 6 hours of agency-approved training each year.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Foster parents must complete at least 6 hours of pre-service training. Agencies often require more; the state suggests 24 hours of parent preparation.
notes: 6-hour minimum and 24-hour suggestion read from secondary summaries; counties and agencies set their own extra hours.

rule_summary: Each applicant and household member aged 18 or over needs a national fingerprint-based criminal records check. Adults who lived in another state in the past five years need an out-of-state registry check.
notes: DCYF guidance document dated 2017; regulations amended since.

rule_summary: A child older than 3 may not share a bedroom with a child of the opposite sex.
notes: From a federal summary; not found in the regulation text in snippets. May be out of date.

rule_summary: Since the 2020 redesign, board rates are tiered by the child's level-of-need assessment and paid on the 15th of each month. A state release gave an average of 530 dollars a month including clothing.
notes: Press release undated in results; may predate 2025. Tier amounts not found.

rule_summary: No more than five foster and pre-adoptive children in a home, and no more than seven children in total, counting biological, adopted, foster and pre-adoptive children.
notes: Justia copy current through September 2024. Five-child foster limit also applies. Each home's capacity is assessed individually.

rule_summary: A provider agency states that applicants may rent, own their home or live in an apartment.
notes: Provider page, not the regulation.

rule_summary: Kinship caregivers aged 18 to 20 may be considered for a licence.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Every licensed foster home is re-evaluated and re-licensed every two years.
notes: Read from a DCYF policy document summary.

rule_summary: A foster care and adoption licence lets a carer move between fostering and adopting without a new home study or extra training.
notes: Read from federal summary.

rule_summary: A caregiver must be at least 21. A kinship caregiver aged 18 to 20 may be considered. Rhode Island issues a combined foster care and adoption licence.
notes: Read from search summary. A proposed amendment to Part 3 was filed 19 March 2025; unclear whether adopted.

rule_summary: A provider agency states that single applicants are eligible.
notes: Provider page, not the regulation.

rule_summary: Licensed foster parents must receive at least 8 hours of DCYF-approved in-service training each year.
notes: From a federal summary of the regulation; may be out of date.

rule_summary: All resource parents complete a 30-hour pre-service orientation, usually 3 hours a week over 10 weeks.
notes: Other sources give 33 or 20 to 30 hours. Curriculum not named.

rule_summary: The monthly subsidy is negotiated between DSS and the adoptive parents. Title IV-E eligible children get Medicaid in any state; state-funded cases may not if the new state has no agreement. Supplemental benefits need prior approval.
notes: Read from search summary; upper limit of the subsidy range was cut off. A 2017 subsidy chart may be out of date.

rule_summary: DSS can reimburse up to 1,500 dollars of one-time costs of adopting a child with special needs, such as the adoption study and legal and court fees. The family must apply and be notified before finalisation.
notes: One-time cap, so no monthly value recorded. Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants go through criminal record and central registry background checks.
notes: Read from search summary. Who in the household is checked was not shown. Child Welfare Information Gateway has a state summary on background checks.

rule_summary: Each child in care must have their own bed and storage space. No child may routinely share a bed or bedroom with an adult, except a child under 1.
notes: Read from search summary of the regulation.

rule_summary: Regular foster care monthly rates from 1 July 2025: 700 dollars for ages 0 to 5, 818 dollars for ages 6 to 12, 863 dollars for ages 13 to 20.
notes: Value is the lowest age band (0 to 5). Earlier 2022 rate was 619 dollars for ages 0 to 5.

rule_summary: DSS does not charge a fee to become a licensed foster parent or an approved adoptive parent.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants complete a home safety inspection, including a fire inspection.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A home study is part of licensing and adoptive approval. The model used was not shown in search results.
notes: Child Welfare Information Gateway summary dated 2018; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Foster parents may rent their home; they do not have to own it. Proof of home or tenant insurance is required.
notes: Read from search summary. Landlord consent rule not seen.

rule_summary: Applicants must show sufficient income to meet the needs of their family and any children placed with them.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A private agency document refers to an initial two-year licensing period. No state source for the term was seen.
notes: Unverified; read from search summary of an agency-hosted document. Check R. 114-550.

rule_summary: Most foster parents are licensed through private child-placing agencies; DSS licenses directly in some circumstances. Kinship foster care licensing is also offered.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants for a foster home licence or adoptive home approval must be at least 21. For a kinship carer aged 18 to 21, the age rule may be waived if a spouse or partner aged 21 or over lives in the home.
notes: Read from search summary of the regulation. One private agency blog states 18; regulation states 21.

rule_summary: Foster parents may be single, married or in a committed relationship.
notes: Read from search summary of the DSS FAQ.

rule_summary: A DSS brochure says applicants should be licensed within four months.
notes: Read from search summary of a March 2025 brochure.

rule_summary: Each foster parent must complete at least 14 hours of training each year, or 28 hours before each relicensure.
notes: Read from search summary of the regulation.

rule_summary: Each foster parent must complete at least 14 hours of preservice training, including licensing requirements and standards of care, before licensure.
notes: Read from search summary of the regulation. A DSS-related summary gives 15 hours; private agencies may require more (one states 32). Sources differ.

rule_summary: Applicants must provide proof of automobile insurance.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Children with special needs can get adoption assistance negotiated at placement, and Medicaid until 18. One-time adoption costs are covered up to 2,000 dollars per child. Maintenance runs to 18, or 19 if in secondary school.
notes: Child Welfare Information Gateway gives 1,500 dollars for one-time costs; sources differ. Age 18/19 rule from ARSD 67:14:14.

rule_summary: A criminal record check covers the prospective foster parent and every other adult in the home. Household members aged 10 and over are screened for substantiated abuse or neglect.
notes: Read from a Child Welfare Information Gateway summary. Fingerprint checks were confirmed only for adoptive parents (FBI check before an adoptive placement).

rule_summary: Family foster homes must have enough sleeping space to accommodate a child in care and the carer's own family comfortably.
notes: Read from search summary; detailed sub-rules were not shown.

rule_summary: Foster care payment rates are set in the administrative rule on foster care rates. The current amount was not confirmed from an official source.
notes: Unverified: one search summary cited a daily rate of 22.85 dollars from an undated news item; not recorded as a value.

rule_summary: If both spouses work outside the home, a child care plan must be approved.
notes: Read from a 2018 summary.

rule_summary: Each household member under 18 must meet Department of Health immunisation requirements.
notes: Read from a 2018 summary.

rule_summary: A home study is required for licensing. The model used was not shown in search results.
notes: Child Welfare Information Gateway summary dated February 2018; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Applicants must have income that meets the needs of the existing family, independent of foster care maintenance payments.
notes: Read from a 2018 summary; may be out of date.

rule_summary: A licensed kinship care pathway has been approved, with lighter training requirements than standard foster licensing and payment at the same rate as foster families.
notes: Read from a news report; effective date and rule citation not seen.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be 21 years of age.
notes: Read from a search summary; unclear which DSS page carried the statement. Rule text on age (ARSD 67:42:01:06 is cross-referenced) not seen.

rule_summary: General qualifications for family foster care providers are set in ARSD 67:42:05:06, which refers to baseline criteria in 67:42:01:06.
notes: Content of the criteria was not shown in search results.

rule_summary: Licensed foster parents must complete at least 6 hours of approved training each year before licence renewal. Carers of a child with a disability or medical, behavioural or emotional disorder need 12 more hours.
notes: Read from search summary. Renewal before each annual renewal implies a yearly licence but this was not confirmed.

rule_summary: Applicants must complete at least 30 hours of orientation training before an initial licence. DSS offers it as classroom and online sessions, and it can be done fully online.
notes: Read from search summary. Curriculum name not confirmed; a DSS staff training plan mentions PRIDE online but that is not shown to be the foster parent curriculum.

rule_summary: Adoption assistance payments may not exceed the DCS foster care board rate and are set as a daily rate. One-time non-recurring adoption costs are reimbursed up to 1,500 dollars per adoptive placement. DCS may adjust rates across the board.
notes: Read from a May 2025 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary and an agency document; DCS policy 15.11 not read.

rule_summary: Applicants must be fingerprinted and pass a background check.
notes: Read from search summary. Who in the household is checked was not shown.

rule_summary: Children aged 3 or older may not share the foster parents' bedroom except for brief periods of illness or emotional distress. The home must have enough space for a child.
notes: Read from search summary of a DCS training page; check current DCS policy 16.4.

rule_summary: Daily rates from 1 July 2026: regular foster care 33.38 dollars (ages 0 to 11) and 38.27 dollars (12 and over); special circumstances 36.72 and 42.10 dollars. Kinship carers get 15.37 dollars a day until fully approved.
notes: Rates are daily, so no monthly value recorded. Extraordinary rates are set case by case up to 60 dollars a day.

rule_summary: A foster home may have no more than six foster children, with listed exceptions such as sibling groups. No more than two children under 2, counting the carers' own; with two under 2, no more than four children in all.
notes: Rule chapter covers child-placing agency foster homes. An emergency rule was filed in November 2020; check the current text. DCS-approved homes may follow DCS policy 16.4.

rule_summary: DCS does not charge prospective foster parents to attend TN KEY pre-approval training.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants complete a health exam.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants take part in a home study. Approval standards are in DCS Policy 16.4; kinship approval in Policy 16.20. The model used was not shown.
notes: URL is a DCS chapter 16 policy file from search results; unclear whether it is 16.4 itself.

rule_summary: Applicants may own or rent their home.
notes: Read from search summary. Landlord consent rule not seen.

rule_summary: Applicants must be at least 21. An applicant to foster a sibling or other blood relative must be at least 18. Regions may add requirements based on placement needs.
notes: Read from search summary of the DCS eligibility page.

rule_summary: Foster parents can be single or married, with or without children of their own.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Since March 2024, non-therapeutic foster parents must complete 8 hours of training each year. Therapeutic foster parents must complete 14 hours, 6 of them on therapeutic topics.
notes: Read from search summary. An older 2021 DCS guide lists 15 hours a year; likely out of date.

rule_summary: All potential foster, kinship and adoptive parents must attend 25 hours of TN KEY pre-approval training before approval.
notes: Read from search summary of a TN KEY overview labelled version 23.12.1; hours may have changed.

rule_summary: Adoption assistance can include Medicaid, monthly payments capped by the child's service level at placement, and reimbursement of one-time costs (home study, legal, court, travel). Agreeing to the maximum bars a later appeal.
notes: Nonrecurring cap not confirmed. A family advocacy source gives monthly rates of 400 to 545 dollars; not recorded.

rule_summary: Bedrooms need at least 40 square feet per occupant, with no more than four occupants per bedroom. A single-occupant bedroom needs at least 80 square feet.
notes: Read from a 2018 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary and a search summary of chapter 749; may be out of date.

rule_summary: From 1 September 2025 the minimum daily reimbursement to a foster family is 27.07 dollars at the basic service level and 47.37 dollars at the moderate level.
notes: Rates are daily, so no monthly value recorded. Payment flows through child-placing agencies; T3C pass-through amounts may differ.

rule_summary: A basic foster family home may care for no more than six children, counting the family's own children and any children it provides day care for.
notes: Read from search summary of the DFPS overview.

rule_summary: A home study is required for verification as a foster home and approval as an adoptive home. The model used was not shown.
notes: Child Welfare Information Gateway summary dated 2018; may be out of date.

rule_summary: No rule barring renters was found. A private agency states its families include renters and homeowners.
notes: Unverified; not from a state source. State rule on renting not seen.

rule_summary: Applicants must be financially stable.
notes: Read from search summary. No income figure was shown.

rule_summary: Prospective foster and adoptive parents must be at least 21.
notes: Read from search summary of the DFPS requirements page. Citation from a 2018 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary; chapter 749 has since moved to Title 26.

rule_summary: DFPS rules set out how foster and adoptive home inquiries are taken and screened.
notes: Content of the rule not shown in search results.

rule_summary: Young people adopted from DFPS care with an adoption assistance agreement may qualify for a state college tuition and fee waiver at Texas public colleges and universities.
notes: Eligibility rules differ for adoptions before and after 1 September 2009.

rule_summary: Prospective foster or adoptive parents may be single or married.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Each caregiver must complete annual training hours set in a chart in the rule, within each 12 months after verification. Two foster parents may combine their hours.
notes: The hour chart is a graphic and was not shown in search results. A February 2026 proposed rule package would add training sections; adoption status unknown.

rule_summary: Texas uses NTDC as a 19-hour pre-service training for prospective foster and adoptive parents. Minimum standards also set general pre-service training for caregivers, and agencies may waive parts not relevant to the home.
notes: Sources differ: a 2021 Texas Register table lists 8 hours of general pre-service training plus other required topics.

rule_summary: Payment of nonrecurring adoption expenses may not exceed 2,000 dollars and covers only costs incurred before finalisation. Children with an adoption assistance agreement get Medicaid with no income or asset test.
legal_citation: Utah Code 80-2-806; Utah Admin. Code R512-43-4
notes: Read from search summaries. Medicaid rule from the DHHS Medicaid policy manual. Time-limited supplemental adoption assistance (2 to 6 months) is also offered.

rule_summary: Bedrooms need at least 40 square feet per child (not counting bathrooms or storage), no more than four children per room. Adults may not share a foster child's bedroom. Opposite-gender children may not share unless an exception applies.
notes: Read from search summary. A 2014 rule change reduced square footage rules; check the current text.

rule_summary: Payment criteria for caregivers of children in out-of-home care are set in DCFS rule. Current rate amounts were not found.
notes: Only the section title was seen; amounts not found.

rule_summary: No more than four foster children may live in a licensed foster home, and no more than three in a certified foster home. The limits may be exceeded to place a child with a sibling.
notes: Read from search summary of a copy amended effective 1 May 2024. Copies differ on the wording of the sibling exception. Also in R501-12-5.

rule_summary: Applicants must be in good health and emotionally stable.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A home study is required for licensing. The model used was not shown.
notes: Child Welfare Information Gateway summary dated 2018.

rule_summary: Foster parents are relicensed each year. Some licensees may hold a three-year licence with annual updates; a citation for noncompliance reverts it to one year.
notes: Read from search summaries of R501-12-4 and the Office of Licensing pages.

rule_summary: An individual or a legally married couple aged 21 or over may apply to be a foster parent.
notes: Read from a 2018 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Applicants may be an individual or a legally married couple. A DCFS rule section is titled 'Cohabitation Not Permitted for Foster Parents'.
notes: Only the section title was seen in search results; its content was not read.

rule_summary: A foster parent must live at the licensed location when a foster child is placed with them.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Utah Foster Care's reference sheet says foster parents need to complete 16 hours of training to meet minimum standards. The period covered was cut off in the snippet.
notes: Unverified; time frame unclear. A 2014 rule change removed ongoing training from licensing rules, so this may be a DCFS or contract requirement rather than a licensing rule.

rule_summary: Each applicant must show completion of DCFS or agency-approved pre-service training within the past 24 months, and current CPR and first aid training.
notes: Read from search summary. Number of pre-service hours not found.

rule_summary: Nonrecurring adoption expenses are reimbursed at actual cost up to 2,000 dollars per child per placement. Payment can start once placed and signed. Applications after finalisation are for state-funded maintenance only.
notes: Claim deadline differs: the regulation says within two years of the final decree; a 2025 DSS information sheet says 12 months.

rule_summary: Basic maintenance is paid monthly at uniform state rates by age group, effective July 2022. Enhanced payments above basic maintenance use the VEMAT assessment.
notes: Dollar amounts not shown in search results. A third-party page gives 450 to 700 dollars a month; not recorded.

rule_summary: The number of children in foster care in a foster family home may not exceed six unless specific exemptions apply.
notes: Read from a 2020 Virginia Register entry; may have changed. Section number not shown. Virginia is state-supervised and locally administered; local departments of social services may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: The mutual family assessment covers items such as motivation to foster and adopt, stability of household relationships and financial resources.
notes: Read from a partial search snippet. Model name not recorded. Virginia is state-supervised and locally administered; local departments of social services may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Applicants attend a one-time orientation, complete pre-service training and a home study, and take part in at least three face-to-face interviews.
notes: Value is the minimum number of interviews. Read from an older printer copy of the DSS page; may be out of date. Virginia is state-supervised and locally administered; local departments of social services may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: A relative home can be approved as a foster home and paid state maintenance rates only if it meets foster home provider requirements.
notes: Read from search summary of the September 2024 manual section.

rule_summary: The approval period for a foster or adoptive home provider is 36 months.
notes: Read from search summary. Virginia is locally administered; local departments carry out approvals.

rule_summary: The foster and adoptive home approval standards apply to adoptive home providers until the final adoption order. A resource parent supports reunification and is prepared to adopt if reunification does not happen.
notes: Read from search summary. Virginia is state-supervised and locally administered; local departments of social services may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: No minimum age was found in state regulation or DSS text. Private agency and third-party pages give 21 or 18.
notes: Unverified; sources conflict and none is a state source. UMFS also says there is no upper age limit. Virginia is state-supervised and locally administered; local departments of social services may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: As a condition of reapproval, each provider must complete in-service training. Hours were not shown.
notes: Read from search summary. Virginia is state-supervised and locally administered; local departments of social services may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Providers must complete pre-service training during the initial approval process, including normalcy training added by 2016 law. State hours were not found; local departments often use PRIDE.
notes: Read from search summary. Local hours vary (Fairfax 2018 listed about 15 hours in person and 44 online). Virginia is state-supervised and locally administered; local departments of social services may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: One-time expenses in special needs adoptions are reimbursed up to 2,000 dollars per child. Monthly subsidies are set under DCF policy. Deferred agreements are possible if the family applies before finalisation.
notes: Read from a September 2023 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary.

rule_summary: All household members aged 16 and over are checked through the Vermont court records system and the DCF master index.
notes: Read from a search summary of DCF policy; unclear which policy number holds the rule.

rule_summary: No more than four children may sleep in a bedroom when any is a foster child. No child over 5 may share a room with a child of the opposite sex when either is a foster child.
notes: Read from a 2018 summary; check current rule text.

rule_summary: DCF reviews foster care reimbursement amounts each year. A 2022 legislative document proposed daily rates of 19.64 to 31.20 dollars across three levels.
notes: Proposed rates; unclear whether adopted. Current rates not found.

rule_summary: The number of children allowed depends on the family's ability to supervise and the home's living space. Versions of the rule differ: one caps foster children at four, a later one caps all children in the home at six.
notes: Sources conflict on the cap; no value recorded.

rule_summary: Applicants must show enough income to support the family, not counting foster children, without relying on the foster care reimbursement.
notes: Read from a 2018 summary; may be out of date.

rule_summary: A foster home licence is valid for up to three years if requirements are met.
notes: Read from search summary; unclear which of the listed DCF documents stated it.

rule_summary: Primary caregivers in a foster home must be at least 21.
notes: Read from a February 2018 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary. An archived DCF page also gives 21. Rules have since been revised.

rule_summary: DCF licenses foster homes under 33 V.S.A. 4905. The licensing rules were first adopted in 1992 and have been amended since, including revisions reported after two legal settlements.
notes: Current version unclear; a 2023 rule revision (22-P30) went through the legislative rules committee.

rule_summary: Applicants can be single, married, living with a partner or joined in a civil union.
notes: Read from an archived 2021 copy of the DCF foster care page; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Applicants take an orientation and a foundations course, then Learning Networks training within their first year of licensing. Hours were not shown.
notes: Read from search summary of DCF outreach material.

rule_summary: The adoption support program offers Medicaid, preauthorised counselling, reimbursement of nonrecurring finalisation costs up to 1,500 dollars per child, and a negotiated monthly payment capped by the child's age at adoption.
notes: Read from search summary. Nonrecurring costs are paid after finalisation on receipts.

rule_summary: Every adult in the home completes a Washington State Patrol check and FBI fingerprinting. People 16 or over in the household or with unsupervised contact must pass a check. A criminal history does not automatically disqualify.
notes: Combines the archived 2024 WAC text and the DCYF FAQ. Value is the age from which checks apply.

rule_summary: General bedroom requirements and bedroom sharing rules are set in WAC 110-148-1470 and WAC 110-148-1475.
notes: Content of the sections not seen in search results.

rule_summary: A home licensed with two caregivers may care for up to six children, counting the carers' own under-18s and foster or respite children; a one-caregiver home up to four, with one more foster child at the licensor's discretion.
notes: Read from search summary of the 2024 archived text. WAC 110-148-1390 lets DCYF allow a temporary excess in the child's best interest. Proposed for amendment in WSR 26-08-090.

rule_summary: Homes serving children under 2 must show proof of pertussis and influenza immunisation for everyone living there, with possible medical exceptions.
notes: Read from an archived 2019 WAC copy; may be out of date.

rule_summary: A home study is required, along with home visits and interviews. The model used was not shown.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Foster home licences run on a three-year licensing cycle.
notes: Inferred from the three-year training cycle in DCYF policy; licence term rule itself not seen.

rule_summary: Applicants must be at least 21 to apply for a foster home licence. Exceptions may be made for an 18-year-old relative of the child.
notes: Relative exception from the DCYF FAQ. A 2026 rulemaking (WSR 26-08-090) proposes amending chapter 110-148 WAC; check current text.

rule_summary: Applicants can be single, partnered or married.
notes: Read from search summary of the DCYF FAQ.

rule_summary: Citizenship is not required, but an applicant or co-applicant on the licence must have a taxpayer identification number (such as an ITIN) to receive foster care reimbursement.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Licensed foster parents complete 24 hours of caregiver continuing education every three years, and may carry up to 12 extra hours into the next cycle. An individual in-service training plan is made after licensing.
notes: An older DCYF page gave 36, 30 then 24 hours across successive three-year periods.

rule_summary: Foster and adoptive applicants complete an orientation and pre-service Caregiver Core Training: eight sessions of about three hours, about 27 hours, plus first aid, CPR and bloodborne pathogens training.
notes: Hours from a third-party summary; check DCYF policy 3-20-100. WAC 110-148-1375 is proposed for amendment in WSR 26-08-090.

rule_summary: Adoption assistance can include a monthly subsidy at basic, supplemental and exceptional rates, and a one-time expense reimbursement. Parents may appeal the approved monthly amount.
legal_citation: Wis. Admin. Code DCF 50; Wis. Stat. 48.975
notes: Dollar amounts not found. Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Applicants go through a criminal background check and must meet rules on law violations and other background information.
notes: Read from search summary. Who in the household is checked was not shown.

rule_summary: No more than four children may regularly occupy one bedroom. A foster child aged 6 or over may not regularly share a bedroom with a child of the opposite sex.
notes: CR 25-043 proposes letting a foster child share a bedroom with another child if the supervising agency approves; status unclear. Wisconsin is county-administered (state-run in Milwaukee); county agencies and licensed child-placing agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Uniform foster care basic maintenance rates are age-based, set under Wis. Stat. 48.62(4) and by the 2025-27 budget for 2026 and 2027. Kinship and level 1 payments move to match the age-based foster rates.
notes: Age-band amounts not legible in snippets. Kinship care was listed at 384 dollars a month from 1 January 2026; may be superseded by the budget change.

rule_summary: A licensing agency must apply to the department exceptions panel to place 8 or more children in a foster home to keep siblings together. CR 25-043 proposes a total-occupancy count in a new DCF 56.085.
notes: General cap on foster children per home not confirmed. Wisconsin is county-administered (state-run in Milwaukee); county agencies and licensed child-placing agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: A foster home licence lasts no more than 2 years and may be renewed after relicensing requirements are met.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Foster homes are certified at levels of care 1 to 5. Level 1 is only for a child-specific licence. Level 5 (exceptional treatment) needs notice to the department exceptions panel before applying.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Counties, tribes and private agencies license foster parents in Wisconsin; the state does not license them directly.
notes: Read from search summary. Wisconsin is county-administered (state-run in Milwaukee); county agencies and licensed child-placing agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Nonrelative foster parents must be at least 21 and relative foster parents at least 18. A 2025 proposed rule (CR 25-043) would set one minimum age of 18 for all.
notes: Read from search summary of the proposed rule; unclear whether CR 25-043 has been adopted. Wisconsin is county-administered (state-run in Milwaukee); county agencies and licensed child-placing agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: The DCF become-a-foster-parent page says applicants must be 21 or older.
notes: Read from search summary. Rule text (DCF 56.05) allows relatives from 18; see the min-age row. Wisconsin is county-administered (state-run in Milwaukee); county agencies and licensed child-placing agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Foster parents can be married, single or in unmarried relationships.
notes: Read from search summary. Wisconsin is county-administered (state-run in Milwaukee); county agencies and licensed child-placing agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Initial licensing training minimums depend on level of care: 30 hours for level 2, 24 hours for level 3 and 30 hours for level 4, completed during the initial licensing period.
notes: Value is the level 2 figure. Read from a December 2025 DCF publication of the rule. Level 3 figure of 24 looks out of step with levels 2 and 4; check the text. Wisconsin is county-administered (state-run in Milwaukee); county agencies and licensed child-placing agencies may add their own requirements.

rule_summary: Requirements marked with an asterisk in DCF 56 are ones licensing agencies may grant an exception for.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Adoption assistance payments and benefits may begin at finalisation. West Virginia also has a conditional subsidy programme. Amounts were not found.
notes: Read from search summary. The DoHS Adoption Policy revised June 2025 likely holds the amounts.

rule_summary: All foster parents and everyone in the household must undergo a background check.
notes: Read from a private agency page; state rule section not seen.

rule_summary: A child may not share a bedroom or bed with an adult or a child of the opposite sex; a child under 2 may share a room for a time. Each child needs their own bed, not a cot or roll-away. No more than four children per bedroom.
notes: Combines the Justia copy (current to September 2024) and a July 2025 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary. No square footage standard found.

rule_summary: Certified kinship or relative providers receive the foster care board rate, given as 600 dollars a month per child from certification.
notes: Read from search summary of a July 2025 source; unclear which document. Standard non-relative board rate not confirmed. Non-certified kinship carers get a TANF-based payment.

rule_summary: The total number of children in a foster home, including the family's own children living there, may not exceed six.
notes: Justia copy may not be current. Another version defines a foster family home as caring for five or fewer unrelated children; sources differ.

rule_summary: Agencies must ensure a foster or adoptive home has no health or safety hazards and is clean and comfortable enough to support the family's well-being.
notes: Read from search summary. No bedroom detail was shown.

rule_summary: After registering and attending a pre-service orientation, families complete a home study. DoHS provides home studies for families who plan to foster. The model used was not shown.
notes: Read from search summary; unclear which DoHS document. A Placement Certification Policy revised March 2026 exists.

rule_summary: Applicants need economic stability.
notes: Read from a private agency page; state rule not seen.

rule_summary: A private agency lists a minimum age of 21 to foster.
notes: Unverified; not from a state source. The rule text on age was not seen.

rule_summary: A private agency says any relationship status is welcome: single, married or cohabiting.
notes: Unverified; not from a state source.

rule_summary: Agencies must give foster parents at least 15 hours of ongoing training in the first year of approval and at least 12 hours a year after that, plus first aid and CPR.
notes: Read from a July 2025 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary. Value is the annual hours after year one.

rule_summary: The National Training and Development Curriculum (NTDC) replaced PRIDE as the required pre-service training from 16 October 2025. Training is free.
notes: Unclear which result stated the change; hours under NTDC not confirmed. Older private agency material cites 30 hours.

rule_summary: The amount is based on the child's needs and the adoptive parents' circumstances. One source gives a standard rate of 399 dollars a month, negotiable up to the child's foster care rate.
notes: The 399 dollar figure came from a source updated October 2024, unclear which; not shown in the rule snippet. Unverified.

rule_summary: Applicants must have no criminal history as defined by certification policies.
notes: Read from search summary. Who in the household is checked was not shown.

rule_summary: Bedrooms need at least 75 square feet for the first occupant and 50 for each additional one, with no more than four children per room. Foster parents may never share a bed or bedroom with a child in care.
notes: Read from search summary; rule amended in 2021.

rule_summary: Wyoming pays basic monthly foster care rates in three age brackets, with add-ons for children who need extra care. Current amounts were not found.
notes: From a 2021 Legislative Service Office memo; amounts not shown in snippet.

rule_summary: A child-placing agency foster home may house no more than five foster children, and no more than ten children in all including the foster parents' own.
notes: Applies to CPA foster homes; copy current through April 2019. Cap for DFS-certified homes not confirmed. TFC homes may take no more than two infants under 2.

rule_summary: Applicants must be in good physical and emotional health.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: A home study is required for certification. The model used was not shown.
notes: 2018 summary.

rule_summary: Applicants must be financially stable.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Foster home certification runs in two-year periods.
notes: From a 2020 DFS plan; rule section not seen.

rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 21.
notes: Read from search summary of the DFS FAQ. A 2018 rule summary and the TFC rule (049-6 6-7) also give 21.

rule_summary: The home study requires five positive references for each prospective foster parent.
notes: Value is the number of references. From a 2018 Child Welfare Information Gateway summary; may be out of date.

rule_summary: Singles and couples may apply.
notes: Read from search summary.

rule_summary: Foster parents must complete 36 hours of training in each two-year certification period to be recertified.
notes: From a 2020 DFS recruitment plan. The 2018 rule summary says 18 hours a year; the figures are equal per year but stated differently.

rule_summary: Foster parents complete an 18-hour orientation before working directly with children in care, and hold current CPR and first aid certification. PRIDE may be used to meet the hours.
notes: From a 2018 summary; the 2020 DFS recruitment plan says 18 hours in the certification year and mentions PRIDE.
